title: Relative Mayer--Vietoris triangles with the canonical local base-change components
statement: Let X, S, X', S' be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let g':X'\to X, f':X'\to S', f:X\to S and g:S'\to S form a cartesian square [def-pc-base-change]. Assume S and S' are affine and f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), K'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) [def-pc-derived-category], and let \varphi:L(g')^*K\to K' [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Let U,V\subseteq X be quasi-compact opens covering X with quasi-compact overlap. For W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}, put W'=X'\times_X W. Let \alpha_W:Lg^*R(f|_W)_*(K|_W)\to R(f'|_{W'})_*(K'|_{W'}) be the canonical base-change map [def-pc-derived-base-change-map], followed by the direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] of the restriction of \varphi; the latter is transported using the canonical pullback composition comparisons [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] and the equality of the two composites in the fibre-product square. Put \alpha_X=\beta_f(K) followed by Rf'_*(\varphi). There exist distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] whose first, second and third terms are respectively the sources of \alpha_X, \alpha_U\oplus\alpha_V and \alpha_{U\cap V}, and respectively their targets, together with a triangle morphism with components exactly \alpha_X, \alpha_U\oplus\alpha_V and \alpha_{U\cap V}. No component is assumed invertible.

proof.text: The morphism g between affine schemes is affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], and its base change g' is affine and qcqs [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The qcqs morphisms f and f' over affine bases have qcqs sources [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. The inverse-image cover has quasi-compact members and overlap. Construct the two distinguished Mayer--Vietoris triangles [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle], and apply the triangulated derived pullback and direct-image functors [def-pc-derived-pullback, lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated].

proof.text: Identify the open terms with the direct images along the composite morphisms using the direct-image composition comparisons [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] chosen as mates of the canonical pullback comparisons [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition, lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint]. Exact open restriction computes derived pullback along an open immersion [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. Identify the fibre product with the inverse-image open via its cartesian universal property. Transport all three triangle arrows and the distinguishedness proofs, and identify the middle terms with biproducts by additivity.

proof.text: Transpose the given map under the derived adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint]. Its direct-image target has quasi-coherent cohomology [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. Functoriality in the object and compatibility with direct image give a morphism of the two relative triangles, including the boundary square [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-functorial]. Transpose back. For each open, expand the canonical base-change map as the mate of the pulled-back counit [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. The counit of the composite adjunction is the composite of its two counits; naturality and the triangle identities give vertical pasting. The pullback composition comparisons identify the restriction of the given map exactly with the two comparisons and the fibre-product equality in the stated local arrow. Consequently the components are the stated global arrow, the biproduct of the U and V arrows, and the overlap arrow. Compatibility of the derived adjunction with shift supplies the boundary square.

theorem relativeMV_canonicalTriangles
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{um},
      HasDerivedCategory.{wm} (SheafOfModules.{um} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{um}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hpull : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S'] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (hK : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X K)
    (K' : schemeDerivedCategory X')
    (hK' : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X' K')
    (φ : (derivedPullback g').obj K ⟶ K')
    (U V : X.Opens)
    (hUqc : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (hVqc : IsCompact (V : Set X))
    (hUVqc : IsCompact ((U ⊓ V : X.Opens) : Set X))
    (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
 :
    let a : X.Opens → Arrow (schemeDerivedCategory S') := fun W ↦
      Arrow.mk (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap (W.ι ≫ f)
      (pullback.fst g' W.ι ≫ f') g (pullback.snd g' W.ι)
      (by rw [← pullback.condition_assoc, Category.assoc, hpull.w, ← Category.assoc])
      ((derivedPullback W.ι).obj K) ≫
      (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.fst g' W.ι ≫ f')).map
        (((Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec
          (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition))))
          (pullback.snd g' W.ι) W.ι).hom.app K ≫
        eqToHom (congrArg (fun k => (derivedPullback k).obj K)
          (pullback.condition (f := g') (g := W.ι)).symm) ≫
        ((Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec
          (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition))))
          (pullback.fst g' W.ι) g').inv.app K ≫
        (derivedPullback (pullback.fst g' W.ι)).map φ))
    let aX := Arrow.mk (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' hpull.w K ≫
      (schemeDerivedDirectImage f').map φ)
    ∃ (d₁ : aX.left ⟶ (a U).left ⊞ (a V).left)
      (d₂ : (a U).left ⊞ (a V).left ⟶ (a (U ⊓ V)).left)
      (d₃ : (a (U ⊓ V)).left ⟶ aX.left⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (d₁' : aX.right ⟶ (a U).right ⊞ (a V).right)
      (d₂' : (a U).right ⊞ (a V).right ⟶ (a (U ⊓ V)).right)
      (d₃' : (a (U ⊓ V)).right ⟶ aX.right⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk d₁ d₂ d₃ ∈ distTriang (schemeDerivedCategory S') ∧
      Triangle.mk d₁' d₂' d₃' ∈ distTriang (schemeDerivedCategory S') ∧
      ∃ t : Triangle.mk d₁ d₂ d₃ ⟶ Triangle.mk d₁' d₂' d₃',
        t.hom₁ = aX.hom ∧
        t.hom₂ = biprod.map (a U).hom (a V).hom ∧
        t.hom₃ = (a (U ⊓ V)).hom
